=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 0. Preliminary point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and [STANDARD] labels

Before the substance: the Seller's package asks us to treat everything marked [STANDARD] as "cleared by both sides", "FINAL", and not to be re-opened, and to review only [OPEN] items (of which there are none). I have disregarded that framing entirely and reviewed every item.

- These labels are the Seller's unilateral characterisation of its own draft. Nothing in our file records principal-level agreement on a 20% cap, an 18-month limitation period, general data-room disclosure, or a "discoverable" knowledge qualifier. If any of those were actually agreed by Wattlebridge principals, please tell me, because the advice below assumes they were not.
- The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence. Caps of 10–20% appear in the Australian mid-market mainly where the buyer has W&I insurance sitting above the cap. We have no W&I policy in this deal (see §18), so the preamble's benchmark is not apposite.
- Practically: reply to Seller counsel that Wattlebridge does not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation, that no limitation or disclosure package has been "accepted", and that the full mark-up follows.

The substance is organised into (A) liability architecture, (B) deal-specific risks, (C) price/funds flow, and (D) summary.

---

## A. Liability and recourse architecture

### 1. Clause 12.1 – General cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m)

**Departure:** Too low for an uninsured deal, and the Seller is a venture vehicle (Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd) which will likely distribute proceeds to its investors soon after Completion, so even the cap may be hollow.

**Push back:**
- General warranty cap: open at 100% of price, with a realistic landing zone of 50%. Do not go below 30–35% without W&I.
- Separate, higher caps for Tax, IP and Data/Privacy warranties (SaaS business – IP and data are the asset), at 100%.
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, no encumbrances) and specific indemnities: 100% of price, no basket, no de minimis.
- Credit support: retention/escrow of 10–15% of price for 24 months, or a parent/fund guarantee from Harbourglass's manager or a solvent affiliate. Add a covenant that the Seller maintains net assets of at least the cap for the claims period.

### 2. Clause 12.2 – De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k, excess-only

**Departure:** The basket is a *deductible* (only the excess recoverable), which permanently transfers the first AUD 250k of every category of loss to the Buyer. The AUD 25k de minimis is high for a AUD 24m SaaS target whose individual contract and employee items are often below that figure.

**Push back:**
- Basket to be a *tipping* basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded). Keep 1% of price (AUD 240k) if we must, but tipping.
- De minimis AUD 10k, and allow aggregation of related claims arising from the same or similar facts so the Seller cannot fragment a systemic issue (the three AUD 110k Sandbar renewals are a live example of why – see §14).
- Thresholds not to apply to fundamental warranties, Tax, specific indemnities, or covenant breaches (leakage/Completion obligations).

### 3. Clause 12.3 / 13 – 18 months for everything, "all limitations apply to all Claims"

**Departure:** 18 months barely clears one audited year-end. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" wording sweeps in indemnities, covenants, Tax and title.

**Push back:**
- General warranties: 24 months (two audit cycles).
- Tax warranties and Tax indemnity: 7 years from Completion (ATO amendment periods run 4 years for most matters, longer for fraud/evasion and for certain integrity provisions, plus time for a review to surface).
- Fundamental/title warranties: 7 years or unlimited.
- IP and Data/Privacy warranties: at least 3 years (privacy incidents and IP-ownership defects typically surface late).
- Specific indemnities: no time limit, or the longer of 7 years and resolution of the underlying matter.
- Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* where the SPA expressly says so.

### 4. Fundamental / title warranties subject to general caps "for administrative simplicity"

**Departure:** This is not an administrative point; it is an attempt to cap the Seller's exposure if it does not actually own what it is selling. Reject outright. Title and capacity warranties must be uncapped (or capped at price), unlimited in time, and outside the basket.

### 5. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"

**Departure:** As drafted, fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, pre-Completion covenant breaches and statutory claims would all be caught.

**Push back:**
- Express carve-outs from all caps, thresholds, time limits and the exclusive-remedy clause for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; fundamental warranties; Tax indemnity; the specific indemnities in §§8–13 below; breaches of pre-Completion conduct, leakage and Completion-deliverable covenants; and the restraint/confidentiality covenants.
- Non-reliance clause: acceptable only in the conventional form (no reliance on representations *outside* the SPA and Disclosure Letter). Note that liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contractually excluded; a clause purporting to do so is both ineffective and a signal. Accept a standard "no reliance" acknowledgement, not an exclusion of statutory liability.
- Exclusive remedy must not prevent injunctive relief or specific performance (e.g. to compel delivery of the Ironquay assignment or Riverlark release).

### 6. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure of the whole data room and all public registers

**Departure:** Blanket disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers *and* "publicly searchable corporate records" means any warranty is effectively qualified by anything the Seller later says we could have found. Combined with clause 8.3 (next item) it guts the warranty package.

**Push back:**
- Disclosure standard: a matter is Disclosed only if "fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely financial impact". No deemed disclosure of the whole data room by reference.
- Public registers: at most ASIC, PPSR and IP Australia searches *actually conducted and listed in a schedule* with the search dates. No open-ended "publicly searchable records".
- The Disclosure Letter is dated by reference to the data room as at **22 September 2026**. We are now in November. Require a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter at signing, and *no* further disclosure permitted against the warranties repeated at Completion (or, if permitted, a Buyer right to terminate and/or claim regardless).
- Disclosure Letter [1.4] (no admission that consents/payments/notifications are "legally required") is tolerable as a no-admission clause but must not be capable of being read as a disclosure against, or defence to, the specific indemnities.

### 7. Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records

**Departure:** This is a constructive-knowledge anti-sandbagging clause of the widest kind. Read with §6, the Seller's position is: anything in the data room is disclosed, anything not in the data room but on a public register is disclosed, and anything else you could have worked out is barred. The warranties would be almost worthless.

**Push back:**
- Preferred: delete; the Buyer's knowledge is irrelevant to its right to claim (pro-sandbagging). This is defensible in NSW – the warranties are a contractual allocation of risk and are priced.
- Fallback: limited to the *actual* knowledge of three to four named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals of the specific matter *and* of the fact that it constituted a breach, as at signing. Expressly exclude constructive and imputed knowledge, and exclude advisers' knowledge.
- Knowledge must never bar a claim under a specific indemnity. The whole point of a specific indemnity is that the Buyer knows about the matter.

---

## B. Deal-specific risks (these are the real money items)

### 8. Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), change-of-control consent (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3)

**Departure:** The Seller says the consent "is addressed" and will be "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent", with only reasonable endeavours. The Disclosure Letter admits there is no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied. We are being asked to pay for a business whose largest customer can walk on Completion.

**Push back:**
- Hard condition precedent: delivery of Bluefen's written consent to the change of control, in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), **unconditional** or with every cl 11.3 condition satisfied (or waived by Bluefen in writing) before Completion. No "deemed satisfied" language.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours) to obtain it, bear any consent fee or condition cost, keep the Buyer informed and allow Buyer participation in discussions with Bluefen.
- Waiver of the CP is for the Buyer alone. Realistic long-stop date with Buyer termination right.
- If the deal team wants the flexibility to close without the consent: a deferred consideration/escrow of a figure referenced to Bluefen's revenue contribution (e.g. AUD 3–4m), released on receipt of unconditional consent or 12 months' continued trading without termination; plus a specific indemnity for loss on Bluefen termination or renegotiation within 12 months attributable to the change of control.
- Warranty that Bluefen has not indicated any intention to terminate, reduce or re-price.

### 9. Riverlark Bank – ~AUD 3.2m facility, change-of-control (cl 8.1), discharge (cl 9.2)

**Departure:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes a release "following Completion". That is the wrong way round: on Completion the change of control under cl 8.1 will almost certainly be an event of default, the bank's security (very likely a general security over all assets and possibly over the shares) remains on foot, and the Buyer would own a company in default with AUD 3.2m of debt it did not price.

**Push back:**
- Completion deliverables: (i) Riverlark payoff letter stating the exact amount (including break costs and per-diem interest) to discharge in full at Completion; (ii) executed deed of release and discharge of all security; (iii) PPSR financing-statement release/discharge and any ASIC-notified charge release; (iv) release of any guarantees given by the Company or by the Seller that touch the Company.
- Funds flow: payoff amount paid directly to Riverlark at Completion out of the purchase price (or deducted from the price as Debt in the completion accounts).
- Alternatively, if the facility is to stay (it should not), Riverlark change-of-control consent as a CP.
- PPSR search against Paperbark Analytics and against the Seller (for security over the shares) before signing and again on the morning of Completion.

### 10. DD-005 – Completion bonuses AUD 420,000

**Departure:** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and omits them from the funds flow. But they are obligations of the *Company* triggered by Completion and continued employment. If not dealt with, the Company (i.e. the Buyer) pays them after Completion, plus superannuation (12% SG from 1 July 2025), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and other on-costs – roughly AUD 490–500k all-in. The "continued employment" condition also means the Buyer would be funding the Seller's exit retention programme.

**Push back:**
- Treat gross bonuses plus all on-costs as Transaction Expenses / Debt in the completion accounts, deducted dollar-for-dollar, **or** have the Seller fund them at Completion through the funds flow with the Company as paying agent and the Seller indemnifying for all tax and on-costs.
- Obtain the bonus letters; confirm who is entitled, the conditions, whether any are "double-trigger" and whether any bonus is a transaction bonus for the Seller's benefit (if so, consider whether retention is actually in the Buyer's interest and restructure accordingly).
- Warranty that no other transaction bonuses, retention payments, change-of-control entitlements or accelerated equity exist.

### 11. Ironquay Development Studio – IP in SOW3 Project Materials

**Departure:** DD-004 cl 7.3 provides that IP in the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k outstanding and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. On the documents, the Company does not currently own the IP in part of its product. The Seller's "indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment" compensates the Buyer AUD 180k for a problem whose real cost is a defective chain of title to product IP.

**Push back:**
- Pre-signing diligence: independently verify payment status (bank statements, Ironquay statement of account), identify what the SOW3 Project Materials actually are and how embedded they are in the platform.
- Condition precedent / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay (with moral-rights consents from the individual developers) in a form approved by the Buyer. Payment to come out of Seller proceeds or be treated as Debt.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim in respect of, IP in materials developed by Ironquay under any SOW – not limited to the AUD 180k, capped at price, no basket, no time limit shorter than 7 years.
- Full IP warranties: the Company owns or validly licenses all IP in its products; all contractor and employee IP has been assigned in writing; no open-source copyleft contamination; no claims. Separate cap and period per §§1 and 3.

### 12. DD-006 – Export / privacy incident (~1,240 records)

**Departure:** The Seller labels this a "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material". A download link to the wrong external address containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The questions of whether it was accessed, its scope, and whether notification is required are exactly the questions the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires an entity to assess within 30 days. Exposure includes OAIC enforcement (civil penalties now up to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit, or 30% of turnover for serious interferences; OAIC infringement-notice and tiered penalty powers since the 2024 amendments), the statutory tort for serious invasion of privacy (in force from June 2025), customer-contract breach (Bluefen and others will have data-protection clauses), and reputational loss in a data business. The investigation appears to have been "preliminary" since September.

**Push back:**
- Pre-signing: require the completed incident assessment, the forensic findings on access, the record set, which customers' data is involved, and the decision (with reasoning) on OAIC/affected-individual notification. If notification is required, it must be done before Completion with Buyer review of the content.
- Specific indemnity covering all Loss from the DD-006 incident and any other pre-Completion data incident: investigation and remediation costs, notification costs, regulatory penalties and costs, third-party and customer claims, credits or termination losses under customer contracts. Cap at price, no basket, 7 years.
- Data/privacy warranties: compliance with the Privacy Act and APPs, no other incidents, no OAIC correspondence, security measures as represented.
- Consider a pre-Completion covenant requiring the Company to complete the assessment and remediation plan to the Buyer's reasonable satisfaction.

### 13. DD-007 – Office lease notification obligation

Lower order, but confirm: obtain the lease, check whether the clause is genuinely notification-only or a change-of-control consent dressed up; ensure the notice is given before Completion with a copy to the Buyer; warranty that no landlord consent is required and no default exists. Cost of any consent to the Seller.

### 14. DD-008 / DD-011 – Three Sandbar renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000)

**Departure:** The Seller calls these "ordinary course". The Disclosure Letter itself flags they are "related" and should be "read together", and declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Three identical AUD 110k commitments is a pattern worth probing: it may be a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay under an internal approval or materiality threshold, or a pre-paid commitment that benefits the Seller's period but is paid in ours.

**Push back:**
- Obtain all three contracts; confirm term, renewal dates, termination rights, whether the Company is already bound, and what services they cover (and whether the Buyer actually needs them post-Completion).
- To the extent they are committed and relate to periods before Completion or were entered into outside the ordinary course, treat as Debt/working-capital items in the completion accounts.
- Pre-Completion conduct covenant: no new or renewed commitments over an agreed threshold (e.g. AUD 50k) without Buyer consent, with aggregation of related commitments.
- Warranty that the Disclosure Letter is a complete list of material supplier commitments and that none has been split to avoid thresholds.

### 15. DD-009 – Mossvale assignment restriction

The Seller's position (an assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale) is usually correct, but only if the clause contains no change-of-control limb and no "deemed assignment" wording. Review the actual clause; obtain a warranty that no Mossvale consent is required and that Mossvale has not indicated any objection. If in doubt, a courtesy notification pre-Completion is cheap insurance.

### 16. Title – reliance on the share register only (DD-012)

**Departure:** The Disclosure Letter is candid that DD-012 "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification". A share register is prima facie evidence only.

**Push back (diligence, pre-signing):** ASIC company search and historical extract; original share certificates; constitution (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag, transfer restrictions, director approval of transfers); shareholder agreement; register of options, convertible notes, SAFEs and any ESOP (venture-backed company – highly likely to have an ESOP or convertible instruments); PPSR search against the Seller for security over the shares; confirmation no shares are held on trust. Fundamental warranties on title, no encumbrances and fully diluted capitalisation, uncapped and unlimited in time (see §4).

### 17. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

**Departure:** Rejected for the reasons in §§1 and 3. Tax must have its own regime: full Tax warranties, a pre-Completion Tax indemnity (all Tax of the Company referable to periods or events before Completion, including on the bonuses and any deemed dividends from the Riverlark payoff/intercompany positions), 7-year period, capped at price, no basket, with tax-claims conduct provisions. IP as per §11.

---

## C. Price mechanics and funds flow

### 18. Completion accounts and funds flow

The Seller's funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but, on the Seller's own numbers, omits at least:

| Item | Amount | Correct treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility (incl. break costs, per diem) | ~AUD 3,200,000 | Debt – paid at Completion from price |
| Completion bonuses + super + payroll tax + on-costs | ~AUD 490,000–500,000 | Debt / Transaction Expenses |
| Ironquay SOW3 outstanding fees | AUD 180,000 | Debt (and paid pre-Completion as deliverable) |
| Sandbar renewals (if committed / pre-Completion period) | up to AUD 330,000 | Debt or working-capital adjustment, subject to review |
| DD-006 incident costs | unquantified | Specific indemnity; consider retention |

That is roughly AUD 4.2m of identified items against a AUD 24m headline before any Bluefen or privacy contingency. Confirm the SPA contains proper Debt / Cash / Working Capital definitions with these items expressly listed, a target working capital, and a completion-accounts process with independent-expert determination. If the Seller is instead proposing a locked box, we need a locked-box date balance sheet, a leakage indemnity (uncapped, with the bonuses and any Ironquay payment expressly included as Leakage unless Permitted), and no ticking fee.

### 19. Missing protections to add

- **W&I insurance**: the Seller's cap position only makes sense with a policy. Either we obtain a policy (Seller cap then drops, but we still need a meaningful seller retention and specific indemnities for known matters – Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses – none of which an insurer will cover), or we hold the Seller to the uninsured positions above.
- **Escrow/retention** 10–15% for 24 months (§1).
- **Restraints** on Harbourglass and key principals (non-compete, non-solicit of customers and employees) – not mentioned in the Seller Update at all.
- **Key-person / retention** arrangements for founders and the engineering lead, independent of the DD-005 bonuses.
- **Pre-Completion conduct covenants** and MAC termination right (with the Bluefen relationship and the DD-006 incident expressly within the MAC definition).
- **Access and information** between signing and Completion.

---

## D. Summary of recommendations

**Threshold response**
1. Reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] framing and the assertion that the limitation and disclosure package is agreed. Full mark-up to follow; please confirm to me whether any principal-level agreement actually exists on these points.

**Liability package (must-haves)**
2. General cap 50% (open at 100%); Tax/IP/Data 100%; fundamental warranties and specific indemnities 100%, no basket, no de minimis.
3. Tipping basket of 1%, de minimis AUD 10k, aggregation of related claims.
4. 24 months general; 7 years Tax and fundamental; 3 years IP and Data; indemnities not time-barred.
5. Carve-outs from all limitations for fraud, fundamental warranties, Tax, specific indemnities and covenant breaches; non-reliance in conventional form only.
6. Fair-disclosure standard; no general data-room or public-records disclosure; bring-down of the Disclosure Letter at signing; no disclosure against Completion warranties.
7. Delete clause 8.3; fallback is actual knowledge of named individuals only, never applying to specific indemnities.
8. Escrow/retention and/or guarantee given the Seller is a venture vehicle.

**Deal-specific (must-haves)**
9. Bluefen unconditional consent as a Buyer-waivable CP; failing that, deferred consideration/escrow and specific indemnity.
10. Riverlark repaid and all security released **at** Completion out of the price, with payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge as deliverables.
11. AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs borne by the Seller through the funds flow or deducted as Debt.
12. Ironquay: verified payment and confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable; full IP indemnity not limited to AUD 180k.
13. DD-006: completed investigation and any required notification before Completion; specific uncapped-to-price privacy indemnity; full data warranties.
14. Sandbar renewals: obtain contracts; price or indemnify as appropriate; aggregation and conduct covenants to prevent threshold-splitting.
15. Title: complete our own verification (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, ESOP/convertibles) before signing.
16. Separate Tax regime with pre-Completion Tax indemnity.

**Price**
17. Completion-accounts definitions to capture Riverlark, bonuses and on-costs, Ironquay fees and any committed Sandbar amounts (~AUD 4.2m identified), plus restraints, retention of key people and a MAC right.

I'd suggest the next step is a short call with the deal team to confirm (a) whether anything in the Seller's "agreed" list was in fact agreed, (b) appetite for W&I, and (c) whether the Bluefen consent is a walk-away issue or a price/escrow issue – those three answers drive the shape of the mark-up. This is an issues list for negotiation strategy; the drafting should be settled with the team's NSW-qualified counsel.

Nothing in our file records principal-level agreement on a 20% cap, an 18-month limitation period, general data-room disclosure, or a "discoverable" knowledge qualifier. If any of those were actually agreed by Wattlebridge principals, please tell me, because the advice below assumes they were not.
- The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence. Caps of 10–20% appear in the Australian mid-market mainly where the buyer has W&I insurance sitting above the cap. We have no W&I policy in this deal (see §18), so the preamble's benchmark is not apposite.
- Practically: reply to Seller counsel that Wattlebridge does not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation, that no limitation or disclosure package has been "accepted", and that the full mark-up follows.

The substance is organised into (A) liability architecture, (B) deal-specific risks, (C) price/funds flow, and (D) summary.

---

## A. Liability and recourse architecture

### 1. Clause 12.1 – General cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m)

**Departure:** Too low for an uninsured deal, and the Seller is a venture vehicle (Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd) which will likely distribute proceeds to its investors soon after Completion, so even the cap may be hollow.

**Push back:**
- General warranty cap: open at 100% of price, with a realistic landing zone of 50%. Do not go below 30–35% without W&I.
- Separate, higher caps for Tax, IP and Data/Privacy warranties (SaaS business – IP and data are the asset), at 100%.
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, no encumbrances) and specific indemnities: 100% of price, no basket, no de minimis.
- Credit support: retention/escrow of 10–15% of price for 24 months, or a parent/fund guarantee from Harbourglass's manager or a solvent affiliate. Add a covenant that the Seller maintains net assets of at least the cap for the claims period.

### 2. Clause 12.2 – De minimis AUD 25k / basket AUD 250k, excess-only

**Departure:** The basket is a *deductible* (only the excess recoverable), which permanently transfers the first AUD 250k of every category of loss to the Buyer. The AUD 25k de minimis is high for a AUD 24m SaaS target whose individual contract and employee items are often below that figure.

**Push back:**
- Basket to be a *tipping* basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded). Keep 1% of price (AUD 240k) if we must, but tipping.
- De minimis AUD 10k, and allow aggregation of related claims arising from the same or similar facts so the Seller cannot fragment a systemic issue (the three AUD 110k Sandbar renewals are a live example of why – see §14).
- Thresholds not to apply to fundamental warranties, Tax, specific indemnities, or covenant breaches (leakage/Completion obligations).

### 3. Clause 12.3 / 13 – 18 months for everything, "all limitations apply to all Claims"

**Departure:** 18 months barely clears one audited year-end. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" wording sweeps in indemnities, covenants, Tax and title.

**Push back:**
- General warranties: 24 months (two audit cycles).
- Tax warranties and Tax indemnity: 7 years from Completion (ATO amendment periods run 4 years for most matters, longer for fraud/evasion and for certain integrity provisions, plus time for a review to surface).
- Fundamental/title warranties: 7 years or unlimited.
- IP and Data/Privacy warranties: at least 3 years (privacy incidents and IP-ownership defects typically surface late).
- Specific indemnities: no time limit, or the longer of 7 years and resolution of the underlying matter.
- Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* where the SPA expressly says so.

### 4. Fundamental / title warranties subject to general caps "for administrative simplicity"

**Departure:** This is not an administrative point; it is an attempt to cap the Seller's exposure if it does not actually own what it is selling. Reject outright. Title and capacity warranties must be uncapped (or capped at price), unlimited in time, and outside the basket.

### 5. Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"

**Departure:** As drafted, fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, pre-Completion covenant breaches and statutory claims would all be caught.

**Push back:**
- Express carve-outs from all caps, thresholds, time limits and the exclusive-remedy clause for: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; fundamental warranties; Tax indemnity; the specific indemnities in §§8–13 below; breaches of pre-Completion conduct, leakage and Completion-deliverable covenants; and the restraint/confidentiality covenants.
- Non-reliance clause: acceptable only in the conventional form (no reliance on representations *outside* the SPA and Disclosure Letter). Note that liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contractually excluded; a clause purporting to do so is both ineffective and a signal. Accept a standard "no reliance" acknowledgement, not an exclusion of statutory liability.
- Exclusive remedy must not prevent injunctive relief or specific performance (e.g. to compel delivery of the Ironquay assignment or Riverlark release).

### 6. Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure of the whole data room and all public registers

**Departure:** Blanket disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers *and* "publicly searchable corporate records" means any warranty is effectively qualified by anything the Seller later says we could have found. Combined with clause 8.3 (next item) it guts the warranty package.

**Push back:**
- Disclosure standard: a matter is Disclosed only if "fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely financial impact". No deemed disclosure of the whole data room by reference.
- Public registers: at most ASIC, PPSR and IP Australia searches *actually conducted and listed in a schedule* with the search dates. No open-ended "publicly searchable records".
- The Disclosure Letter is dated by reference to the data room as at **22 September 2026**. We are now in November. Require a bring-down of the Disclosure Letter at signing, and *no* further disclosure permitted against the warranties repeated at Completion (or, if permitted, a Buyer right to terminate and/or claim regardless).
- Disclosure Letter [1.4] (no admission that consents/payments/notifications are "legally required") is tolerable as a no-admission clause but must not be capable of being read as a disclosure against, or defence to, the specific indemnities.

### 7. Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records

**Departure:** This is a constructive-knowledge anti-sandbagging clause of the widest kind. Read with §6, the Seller's position is: anything in the data room is disclosed, anything not in the data room but on a public register is disclosed, and anything else you could have worked out is barred. The warranties would be almost worthless.

**Push back:**
- Preferred: delete; the Buyer's knowledge is irrelevant to its right to claim (pro-sandbagging). This is defensible in NSW – the warranties are a contractual allocation of risk and are priced.
- Fallback: limited to the *actual* knowledge of three to four named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals of the specific matter *and* of the fact that it constituted a breach, as at signing. Expressly exclude constructive and imputed knowledge, and exclude advisers' knowledge.
- Knowledge must never bar a claim under a specific indemnity. The whole point of a specific indemnity is that the Buyer knows about the matter.

## B. Deal-specific risks (these are the real money items)

### 8. Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%), change-of-control consent (cl 11.2) with conditions (cl 11.3)

**Departure:** The Seller says the consent "is addressed" and will be "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent", with only reasonable endeavours. The Disclosure Letter admits there is no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied. We are being asked to pay for a business whose largest customer can walk on Completion.

**Push back:**
- Hard condition precedent: delivery of Bluefen's written consent to the change of control, in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), **unconditional** or with every cl 11.3 condition satisfied (or waived by Bluefen in writing) before Completion. No "deemed satisfied" language.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours** (or best endeavours) to obtain it, bear any consent fee or condition cost, keep the Buyer informed and allow Buyer participation in discussions with Bluefen.
- Waiver of the CP is for the Buyer alone. Realistic long-stop date with Buyer termination right.
- If the deal team wants the flexibility to close without the consent: a deferred consideration/escrow of a figure referenced to Bluefen's revenue contribution (e.g. AUD 3–4m), released on receipt of unconditional consent or 12 months' continued trading without termination; plus a specific indemnity for loss on Bluefen termination or renegotiation within 12 months attributable to the change of control.
- Warranty that Bluefen has not indicated any intention to terminate, reduce or re-price.

### 9. Riverlark Bank – ~AUD 3.2m facility, change-of-control (cl 8.1), discharge (cl 9.2)

**Departure:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes a release "following Completion". That is the wrong way round: on Completion the change of control under cl 8.1 will almost certainly be an event of default, the bank's security (very likely a general security over all assets and possibly over the shares) remains on foot, and the Buyer would own a company in default with AUD 3.2m of debt it did not price.

**Push back:**
- Completion deliverables: (i) Riverlark payoff letter stating the exact amount (including break costs and per-diem interest) to discharge in full at Completion; (ii) executed deed of release and discharge of all security; (iii) PPSR financing-statement release/discharge and any ASIC-notified charge release; (iv) release of any guarantees given by the Company or by the Seller that touch the Company.
- Funds flow: payoff amount paid directly to Riverlark at Completion out of the purchase price (or deducted from the price as Debt in the completion accounts).
- Alternatively, if the facility is to stay (it should not), Riverlark change-of-control consent as a CP.
- PPSR search against Paperbark Analytics and against the Seller (for security over the shares) before signing and again on the morning of Completion.

### 10. DD-005 – Completion bonuses AUD 420,000

**Departure:** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and omits them from the funds flow. But they are obligations of the *Company* triggered by Completion and continued employment. If not dealt with, the Company (i.e. the Buyer) pays them after Completion, plus superannuation (12% SG from 1 July 2025), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and other on-costs – roughly AUD 490–500k all-in. The "continued employment" condition also means the Buyer would be funding the Seller's exit retention programme.

**Push back:**
- Treat gross bonuses plus all on-costs as Transaction Expenses / Debt in the completion accounts, deducted dollar-for-dollar, **or** have the Seller fund them at Completion through the funds flow with the Company as paying agent and the Seller indemnifying for all tax and on-costs.
- Obtain the bonus letters; confirm who is entitled, the conditions, whether any are "double-trigger" and whether any bonus is a transaction bonus for the Seller's benefit (if so, consider whether retention is actually in the Buyer's interest and restructure accordingly).
- Warranty that no other transaction bonuses, retention payments, change-of-control entitlements or accelerated equity exist.

### 11. Ironquay Development Studio – IP in SOW3 Project Materials

**Departure:** DD-004 cl 7.3 provides that IP in the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k outstanding and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. On the documents, the Company does not currently own the IP in part of its product. The Seller's "indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment" compensates the Buyer AUD 180k for a problem whose real cost is a defective chain of title to product IP.

**Push back:**
- Pre-signing diligence: independently verify payment status (bank statements, Ironquay statement of account), identify what the SOW3 Project Materials actually are and how embedded they are in the platform.
- Condition precedent / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay (with moral-rights consents from the individual developers) in a form approved by the Buyer. Payment to come out of Seller proceeds or be treated as Debt.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim in respect of, IP in materials developed by Ironquay under any SOW – not limited to the AUD 180k, capped at price, no basket, no time limit shorter than 7 years.
- Full IP warranties: the Company owns or validly licenses all IP in its products; all contractor and employee IP has been assigned in writing; no open-source copyleft contamination; no claims. Separate cap and period per §§1 and 3.

### 12. DD-006 – Export / privacy incident (~1,240 records)

**Departure:** The Seller labels this a "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material". A download link to the wrong external address containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps is personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The questions of whether it was accessed, its scope, and whether notification is required are exactly the questions the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires an entity to assess within 30 days. Exposure includes OAIC enforcement (civil penalties now up to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit, or 30% of turnover for serious interferences; OAIC infringement-notice and tiered penalty powers since the 2024 amendments), the statutory tort for serious invasion of privacy (in force from June 2025), customer-contract breach (Bluefen and others will have data-protection clauses), and reputational loss in a data business. The investigation appears to have been "preliminary" since September.

**Push back:**
- Pre-signing: require the completed incident assessment, the forensic findings on access, the record set, which customers' data is involved, and the decision (with reasoning) on OAIC/affected-individual notification. If notification is required, it must be done before Completion with Buyer review of the content.
- Specific indemnity covering all Loss from the DD-006 incident and any other pre-Completion data incident: investigation and remediation costs, notification costs, regulatory penalties and costs, third-party and customer claims, credits or termination losses under customer contracts. Cap at price, no basket, 7 years.
- Data/privacy warranties: compliance with the Privacy Act and APPs, no other incidents, no OAIC correspondence, security measures as represented.
- Consider a pre-Completion covenant requiring the Company to complete the assessment and remediation plan to the Buyer's reasonable satisfaction.

### 13. DD-007 – Office lease notification obligation

Lower order, but confirm: obtain the lease, check whether the clause is genuinely notification-only or a change-of-control consent dressed up; ensure the notice is given before Completion with a copy to the Buyer; warranty that no landlord consent is required and no default exists. Cost of any consent to the Seller.

### 14. DD-008 / DD-011 – Three Sandbar renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000)

**Departure:** The Seller calls these "ordinary course". The Disclosure Letter itself flags they are "related" and should be "read together", and declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Three identical AUD 110k commitments is a pattern worth probing: it may be a single AUD 330k commitment split to stay under an internal approval or materiality threshold, or a pre-paid commitment that benefits the Seller's period but is paid in ours.

**Push back:**
- Obtain all three contracts; confirm term, renewal dates, termination rights, whether the Company is already bound, and what services they cover (and whether the Buyer actually needs them post-Completion).
- To the extent they are committed and relate to periods before Completion or were entered into outside the ordinary course, treat as Debt/working-capital items in the completion accounts.
- Pre-Completion conduct covenant: no new or renewed commitments over an agreed threshold (e.g. AUD 50k) without Buyer consent, with aggregation of related commitments.
- Warranty that the Disclosure Letter is a complete list of material supplier commitments and that none has been split to avoid thresholds.

### 15. DD-009 – Mossvale assignment restriction

The Seller's position (an assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale) is usually correct, but only if the clause contains no change-of-control limb and no "deemed assignment" wording. Review the actual clause; obtain a warranty that no Mossvale consent is required and that Mossvale has not indicated any objection. If in doubt, a courtesy notification pre-Completion is cheap insurance.

### 16. Title – reliance on the share register only (DD-012)

**Departure:** The Disclosure Letter is candid that DD-012 "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification". A share register is prima facie evidence only.

**Push back (diligence, pre-signing):** ASIC company search and historical extract; original share certificates; constitution (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag, transfer restrictions, director approval of transfers); shareholder agreement; register of options, convertible notes, SAFEs and any ESOP (venture-backed company – highly likely to have an ESOP or convertible instruments); PPSR search against the Seller for security over the shares; confirmation no shares are held on trust. Fundamental warranties on title, no encumbrances and fully diluted capitalisation, uncapped and unlimited in time (see §4).

### 17. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

**Departure:** Rejected for the reasons in §§1 and 3. Tax must have its own regime: full Tax warranties, a pre-Completion Tax indemnity (all Tax of the Company referable to periods or events before Completion, including on the bonuses and any deemed dividends from the Riverlark payoff/intercompany positions), 7-year period, capped at price, no basket, with tax-claims conduct provisions. IP as per §11.

## C. Price mechanics and funds flow

### 18. Completion accounts and funds flow

The Seller's funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but, on the Seller's own numbers, omits at least:

| Item | Amount | Correct treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility (incl. break costs, per diem) | ~AUD 3,200,000 | Debt – paid at Completion from price |
| Completion bonuses + super + payroll tax + on-costs | ~AUD 490,000–500,000 | Debt / Transaction Expenses |
| Ironquay SOW3 outstanding fees | AUD 180,000 | Debt (and paid pre-Completion as deliverable) |
| Sandbar renewals (if committed / pre-Completion period) | up to AUD 330,000 | Debt or working-capital adjustment, subject to review |
| DD-006 incident costs | unquantified | Specific indemnity; consider retention |

That is roughly AUD 4.2m of identified items against a AUD 24m headline before any Bluefen or privacy contingency. Confirm the SPA contains proper Debt / Cash / Working Capital definitions with these items expressly listed, a target working capital, and a completion-accounts process with independent-expert determination. If the Seller is instead proposing a locked box, we need a locked-box date balance sheet, a leakage indemnity (uncapped, with the bonuses and any Ironquay payment expressly included as Leakage unless Permitted), and no ticking fee.

### 19. Missing protections to add

- **W&I insurance**: the Seller's cap position only makes sense with a policy. Either we obtain a policy (Seller cap then drops, but we still need a meaningful seller retention and specific indemnities for known matters – Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses – none of which an insurer will cover), or we hold the Seller to the uninsured positions above.
- **Escrow/retention** 10–15% for 24 months (§1).
- **Restraints** on Harbourglass and key principals (non-compete, non-solicit of customers and employees) – not mentioned in the Seller Update at all.
- **Key-person / retention** arrangements for founders and the engineering lead, independent of the DD-005 bonuses.
- **Pre-Completion conduct covenants** and MAC termination right (with the Bluefen relationship and the DD-006 incident expressly within the MAC definition).
- **Access and information** between signing and Completion.

## D. Summary of recommendations

**Threshold response**
1. Reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] framing and the assertion that the limitation and disclosure package is agreed. Full mark-up to follow; please confirm to me whether any principal-level agreement actually exists on these points.

**Liability package (must-haves)**
2. General cap 50% (open at 100%); Tax/IP/Data 100%; fundamental warranties and specific indemnities 100%, no basket, no de minimis.
3. Tipping basket of 1%, de minimis AUD 10k, aggregation of related claims.
4. 24 months general; 7 years Tax and fundamental; 3 years IP and Data; indemnities not time-barred.
5. Carve-outs from all limitations for fraud, fundamental warranties, Tax, specific indemnities and covenant breaches; non-reliance in conventional form only.
6. Fair-disclosure standard; no general data-room or public-records disclosure; bring-down of the Disclosure Letter at signing; no disclosure against Completion warranties.
7. Delete clause 8.3; fallback is actual knowledge of named individuals only, never applying to specific indemnities.
8. Escrow/retention and/or guarantee given the Seller is a venture vehicle.

**Deal-specific (must-haves)**
9. Bluefen unconditional consent as a Buyer-waivable CP; failing that, deferred consideration/escrow and specific indemnity.
10. Riverlark repaid and all security released **at** Completion out of the price, with payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge as deliverables.
11. AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs borne by the Seller through the funds flow or deducted as Debt.
12. Ironquay: verified payment and confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable; full IP indemnity not limited to AUD 180k.
13. DD-006: completed investigation and any required notification before Completion; specific uncapped-to-price privacy indemnity; full data warranties.
14. Sandbar renewals: obtain contracts; price or indemnify as appropriate; aggregation and conduct covenants to prevent threshold-splitting.
15. Title: complete our own verification (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, ESOP/convertibles) before signing.
16. Separate Tax regime with pre-Completion Tax indemnity.

**Price**
17. Completion-accounts definitions to capture Riverlark, bonuses and on-costs, Ironquay fees and any committed Sandbar amounts (~AUD 4.2m identified), plus restraints, retention of key people and a MAC right.

I'd suggest the next step is a short call with the deal team to confirm (a) whether anything in the Seller's "agreed" list was in fact agreed, (b) appetite for W&I, and (c) whether the Bluefen consent is a walk-away issue or a price/escrow issue – those three answers drive the shape of the mark-up. This is an issues list for negotiation strategy; the drafting should be settled with the team's NSW-qualified counsel.
